events.content:
The page now shows a welcome message and logs each view using `after()` from `next/server`, which is Next.js's recommended way to run work after the response is sent. The build passes, and when I ran the production server and requested the page, it returned the welcome heading and then logged the page view with the right user agent.

**`app/page.tsx`** (server component)
- It reads `user-agent` and `referer` from `headers()` while the page renders, then passes those values into the `after()` callback. The Next.js docs say this is required: calling `headers()` or `cookies()` inside `after()` in a server component throws an error at runtime.
- `after()` runs the logging only once the response has finished, so a slow or failing analytics call never delays the page.
- Because it reads request headers, the route is rendered on every request (`ƒ /` in the build output), which is what you want for per-request page views.

**`app/lib/analytics.ts`**
- `logPageView()` sends the event to `ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT` if that environment variable is set. If it isn't set, it prints the event to the console instead.
- Errors are caught and logged, so analytics failures can't affect users.

Two other notes:
- Running `next build` automatically changed `tsconfig.json`: it set `jsx` to `react-jsx` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`. These are standard changes, but they'll show up in your diff.
- If you deploy on serverless outside Vercel, `after()` needs the platform to provide `waitUntil`; on Node.js or Docker it works as is.
